name: Selena Roberts
life: “I still remember the silence before the first floodlight ignites.” On Tuesday, near the bank steps, Selena takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I work nights and never see a blue sky here. I drew the floodlights instead.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a gray fisher's sweater and a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. Selena has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Selena looks down for a moment before saying something difficult during a conversation.
personality: Selena enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To draw the actual night shift lights.
family: Paz Harrow is Selena’s stepsibling. Selena brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Paz checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Paz says, “My little brother still thinks his castle was disqualified because I didn't like it.”
connections: Harold Byrd. They send the night lights and the lunch receipt as two honest views from one shift. Also in the story is Iris Vidal (harbor photographer).
